assumptions.label: Effective inspection radius per dock
assumptions.basis: Engineering assumption, set well inside DJI Dock-class maximum flight radius to reflect useful inspection resolution rather than ferry range. Adjust to match a specific airframe and sensor payload.

assumptions.label: Coverage efficiency
assumptions.basis: Engineering assumption. Pits and pond networks are irregular and terrain interrupts coverage, so a dock never services its full theoretical disc.

assumptions.label: Inspection passes per site per month
assumptions.basis: Operating band spanning monthly to near-daily. No inspection mandate was fetched for this jurisdiction, so no regulatory minimum is asserted.

assumptions.label: Average autonomous mission duration
assumptions.basis: Engineering assumption consistent with a single battery cycle on a dock-based airframe.

assumptions.label: Contracted crew-days per manual inspection pass
assumptions.basis: Engineering assumption for a two-person contracted crew covering a large site on foot or by vehicle. This is the figure to replace with the operator's own contract data during discovery.

assumptions.label: Measured operating footprint
assumptions.basis: Measured from mapped site geometry, not estimated. Each contributing feature is individually citable.

assumptions.label: Discrete operating sites measured
assumptions.basis: Count of mapped features attributed to this operator, excluding features tagged disused or abandoned.

derivation: Measured 49 operating sites totalling 548.482 km² of surface, with 387.45 km of combined boundary. These figures come from mapped geometry, so each one can be opened and checked.
The sites fall into 7 spatial clusters once features within 10 km of each other are grouped. Separated clusters cannot share dock infrastructure, so 7 is the floor on dock count regardless of area.

A dock services roughly 55 km² at a 5 km effective radius, or 19.8 km² at 3 km, after a 70% coverage-efficiency allowance. Dividing measured area by those figures and respecting the cluster floor gives 10 to 28 docks for full coverage.
At 4 to 30 inspection passes per site per month, the programme runs 196 to 1470 autonomous missions monthly, which is 78.4 to 1176 flight hours.

Substituting for contracted crews at 0.5 to 2 crew-days per manual pass, that displaces 98 to 2940 contracted crew-days per month, the hours currently spent putting people on pit walls, haul roads, benches and stockpiles; brine well fields, pond networks, pipework and process plant.

Phase one does not require full coverage. FlytBase's published deployment at the reference account began with a single dock on one zone for one use case at USD 70,000 to 80,000 total system investment, reaching return inside a year, so the first conversation is about one dock on the highest-risk cluster, not 28.
caveats: Footprint is measured from mapped geometry, which reflects the operator's surface disturbance rather than a licensed concession boundary. It is a floor on inspectable area, not a ceiling.
Dock count is a coverage estimate, not a survey. Real placement depends on terrain, line of sight, exclusion zones and available power and network at each location.

Crew-day displacement assumes autonomous passes substitute for manual passes one for one. In practice automation usually increases inspection frequency rather than purely removing labour, which changes the business case from cost saving to risk reduction.
Ranges are shown because every operational input is an assumption until a discovery call replaces it with the operator's own contract and cadence data.
No inspection mandate was fetched for this jurisdiction, so cadence is presented as an operating band with no regulatory minimum claimed.

derivation: Measured 24 operating sites totalling 177.229 km² of surface, with 269.1 km of combined boundary. These figures come from mapped geometry, so each one can be opened and checked.
The sites fall into 7 spatial clusters once features within 10 km of each other are grouped. Separated clusters cannot share dock infrastructure, so 7 is the floor on dock count regardless of area.

A dock services roughly 55 km² at a 5 km effective radius, or 19.8 km² at 3 km, after a 70% coverage-efficiency allowance. Dividing measured area by those figures and respecting the cluster floor gives 7 to 9 docks for full coverage.
At 4 to 30 inspection passes per site per month, the programme runs 96 to 720 autonomous missions monthly, which is 38.4 to 576 flight hours.

Substituting for contracted crews at 0.5 to 2 crew-days per manual pass, that displaces 48 to 1440 contracted crew-days per month, the hours currently spent putting people on pit walls, haul roads, benches and stockpiles; brine well fields, pond networks, pipework and process plant.

Phase one does not require full coverage. FlytBase's published deployment at the reference account began with a single dock on one zone for one use case at USD 70,000 to 80,000 total system investment, reaching return inside a year, so the first conversation is about one dock on the highest-risk cluster, not 9.
caveats: Footprint is measured from mapped geometry, which reflects the operator's surface disturbance rather than a licensed concession boundary. It is a floor on inspectable area, not a ceiling.
Dock count is a coverage estimate, not a survey. Real placement depends on terrain, line of sight, exclusion zones and available power and network at each location.

Crew-day displacement assumes autonomous passes substitute for manual passes one for one. In practice automation usually increases inspection frequency rather than purely removing labour, which changes the business case from cost saving to risk reduction.
Ranges are shown because every operational input is an assumption until a discovery call replaces it with the operator's own contract and cadence data.
No inspection mandate was fetched for this jurisdiction, so cadence is presented as an operating band with no regulatory minimum claimed.

The sites fall into 1 spatial cluster once features within 10 km of each other are grouped. Separated clusters cannot share dock infrastructure, so 1 is the floor on dock count regardless of area.

A dock services roughly 55 km² at a 5 km effective radius, or 19.8 km² at 3 km, after a 70% coverage-efficiency allowance. Dividing measured area by those figures and respecting the cluster floor gives 1 to 1 docks for full coverage.
At 4 to 30 inspection passes per site per month, the programme runs 8 to 60 autonomous missions monthly, which is 3.2 to 48 flight hours.

Substituting for contracted crews at 0.5 to 2 crew-days per manual pass, that displaces 4 to 120 contracted crew-days per month, the hours currently spent putting people on pit walls, haul roads, benches and stockpiles; brine well fields, pond networks, pipework and process plant.

Phase one does not require full coverage. FlytBase's published deployment at the reference account began with a single dock on one zone for one use case at USD 70,000 to 80,000 total system investment, reaching return inside a year, so the first conversation is about one dock on the highest-risk cluster, not 1.
caveats: Footprint is measured from mapped geometry, which reflects the operator's surface disturbance rather than a licensed concession boundary. It is a floor on inspectable area, not a ceiling.
Dock count is a coverage estimate, not a survey. Real placement depends on terrain, line of sight, exclusion zones and available power and network at each location.

Crew-day displacement assumes autonomous passes substitute for manual passes one for one. In practice automation usually increases inspection frequency rather than purely removing labour, which changes the business case from cost saving to risk reduction.
Ranges are shown because every operational input is an assumption until a discovery call replaces it with the operator's own contract and cadence data.
No inspection mandate was fetched for this jurisdiction, so cadence is presented as an operating band with no regulatory minimum claimed.

sqm.headline: SQM is the reference profile this campaign is modelled on. Its measured footprint and disclosed contractor dependency define what a good account looks like.
sqm.whyNow: SQM's own annual filing never uses the words drone, autonomous, automation, while referring to contractors 27 time(s). Automated inspection is absent from the document the company files about its own operations, so there is no incumbent programme to displace and no internal position to argue against. The exposure it would remove, contracted crews at hazardous sites, is disclosed in the same document. Greenfield, evidenced by the company itself rather than by our reading of the market.
sqm.positioning: SQM runs 49 mapped operating areas totalling 548.5 km², and contracted crews currently absorb the exposure of inspecting them on foot. We replace the exposure, not the inspection, same coverage or better, without a person in front of the hazard.
